intro: Each guide is a short job: a product photo, a short ad, a launch clip, a last check, or clothing on a person. You use a photo of your own goods, write your own caption, and post without a shoot.

Open the guide, then open the tool it names. Paste a [product link](page:url-to-video), choose a face in the [actor library](page:ai-actors), or begin from a layout in the [template gallery](page:templates). Downloads do not carry a watermark. [Plans are on the pricing page](page:pricing).

faq.q: Which guide should I open first?
faq.a: Open the one that matches the job in front of you. That is a product photo, a short ad, a launch clip, a check before you publish, or clothing on a person.

faq.q: How do I turn a guide into a file I can post?
faq.a: Pick the guide, then upload a photo of the item you ship. Keep the sentence to something you can show, such as the size on the label. The file you download is the one you post.

faq.q: Why make a short ad instead of waiting on a creator?
faq.a: You can change the opening line and export another file without waiting on a creator's calendar. Book a person when the campaign needs that specific face.

faq.q: Who gets the most from these guides?
faq.a: A person who packs orders and also runs the ads. The guides cover a product photo, a short ad, a launch clip, a last check, and clothing on a person.

faq.q: Can a beginner follow a guide?
faq.a: Yes. If you can photograph the product on a table, you can follow the guide. The tool it names is the only app you open for that file.

faq.q: Which products do the guides cover?
faq.a: Start with [beauty](page:ind-beauty-skincare) or [fashion](page:ind-fashion-clothing). [Food and drinks](page:ind-food-drinks), [home](page:ind-home-living), and [electronics](page:ind-electronics) are here too. The same tools work for other goods you ship.

faq.q: Can I start from photos I already shot?
faq.a: Yes. Start with the photo of the item that actually ships. A logo file is useful only when you are allowed to put that mark on the ad.

faq.q: Which platforms can I post the file to?
faq.a: Use the frame the placement asks for. [Shopify](page:plat-shopify) and [Amazon](page:plat-amazon) want a square photo. A tall 9:16 clip fits [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok) and [YouTube Shorts](page:plat-youtube-shorts). [Instagram](page:plat-instagram) and [Facebook](page:plat-facebook) can take a square still or a tall clip.

faq.q: Do I pay before I can make a file from a guide?
faq.a: Yes. Making the file sits on a paid plan. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits. Pro is $35 for 300. Premium is $63 for 600. The cost shows before every job.

faq.q: Can I put the downloaded file in a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. Put the file on a product page or hand it to a client whose brand you are allowed to show. The [Content Policy](/content) says what you can upload.

faq.q: Why start from a guide instead of a blank file?
faq.a: These guides already decided where the product appears, so your time goes to the claim you can stand behind.

faq.q: How many credits does a photo or a clip cost?
faq.a: A product photo is 24 credits. A 6-second clip is 24, 10 seconds is 40, 15 is 60, and 30 is 120. If a job fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Are the faces in the clip real customers?
faq.a: No. The face is generated for the ad. Do not give that avatar a buyer's name, or a line that says they purchased the product.

steps_h2: How to Make a Post From a Guide in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: You get a file you can post. You type the price in the app you already use.

steps.d: Open the guide that matches the job: a product still, a short ad, or a launch clip.
Upload one clear photo in the tool the guide names. You see the credit cost before it runs.
Save the file, add the price and the caption in the app you already use, then publish it.
